limits: Native failure intentionally abandons completed payloads. Common-heap allocations and resources owned by those payloads can leak; this is current OCCT behavior. The new ordinary constructor does not silently run Rust payload destructors to repair the native leak.

Native oracle allocation count uses real recorded heap nodes; Rust uses the real accumulating allocator outstanding-allocation count. Exact allocation bytes/addresses/backing-block policy and allocator failure exceptions are not equated.

Per-node Rust ownership holds allocator Arc handles absent from native raw links. Proof covers restoration to each implementation own pre-copy handle baseline, not absolute intermediate native handle counts.
Explicit callbacks represent selected native copy policies. Arbitrary C++ copy/move/alias hooks, RTTI/implicit special members, byte layout and destructor exceptions remain unproven.
Rust guard cleanup and test-only raw recovery are not a native API. Native failed-object storage is never inspected, and production Rust exposes no abandoned typed pointer through this adapter.
Assignment into an existing Sequence retains its successful prefix on panic and is intentionally unchanged. Wrapper locks, transient Handle bounds and reentrant access remain separate limitations.
No full-class, denominator-complete or duplicate inherited test/API credit is claimed.
